title: Boss: the report service fails its health checks
summary: Unblock an asyncio event loop with to_thread, then return whatever arrived before a deadline.

steps.title: The ticket
body: Warning  Unhealthy  kubelet  Liveness probe failed: Get "http://10.1.4.17:8000/healthz": context deadline exceeded
Normal   Killing    kubelet  Container reports failed liveness probe, will be restarted
app  WARN  supplier prices: request for slow-b still pending after 30 s
The service is an asyncio app. `/healthz` is trivial, yet it times out while reports are built: the event loop is blocked. And a
slow supplier holds the price page hostage. Both fixes go into `~/reports/report.py` (read `~/reports/README.txt`).

steps.title: 1. Unblock the loop
prompt: `build_reports(names)` calls `render_pdf`, a **blocking** library function, straight from a coroutine. While it runs, nothing else on
the loop runs (the check measures a heartbeat coroutine).
Change `build_reports` so the blocking calls run **off the event loop** and it still returns the file names in order.
Do not change `render_pdf`. Check with `python3 /opt/dojo/files/check_loop.py heartbeat`.

checks.name: the loop keeps running while reports are built
checks.fail: The heartbeat stopped for more than 0.2 s, or the files are wrong. `python3 /opt/dojo/files/check_loop.py heartbeat` shows what happens.

hints: `asyncio.to_thread(fn, *args)` runs a blocking function on a worker thread and lets you await it.
In the loop: `files.append(await asyncio.to_thread(render_pdf, name))`. A `sed -i` on that one line is enough.
explain: `to_thread` is asyncio's `Task.Run`: right for blocking calls you cannot replace. For CPU-heavy Python with the GIL, a process
pool (`loop.run_in_executor(ProcessPoolExecutor(), ...)`) gives real parallelism; a thread only keeps the loop responsive.

steps.title: 2. Whatever arrived by the deadline
prompt: - after `seconds`, **cancel** the ones still running (`asyncio.timeout`) and return `{sku: price}` for the ones that arrived;
- it must not raise because of the timeout.
Check with `python3 /opt/dojo/files/check_loop.py deadline`: two fast suppliers answer in 10 ms, one hangs.

checks.name: the fast prices arrive and the slow one is dropped, on time
checks.fail: Expected the two fast prices within the deadline, with no exception. `python3 /opt/dojo/files/check_loop.py deadline` shows what you return.

checks.name: report.py uses asyncio.timeout
checks.fail: Use `async with asyncio.timeout(seconds):` around the TaskGroup.

hints: Store each price in the dict from an inner coroutine as soon as it arrives; the dict then holds what came in before the deadline.
`try: async with asyncio.timeout(seconds): async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg: ...` then `except TimeoutError: pass` and `return prices`.
solution: src = src[:start] + '''async def prices_by_deadline(skus, get_price, seconds):
explain: When the timeout fires, `asyncio.timeout` cancels the task waiting in the TaskGroup; the group cancels its children and the
cancellation becomes a `TimeoutError` at the `async with`. Results stored before that point stay. This is the asyncio form of the
"time budget with a fallback" from module 3.
